text: The next morning Waythorn left for his office earlier than usual, for he wished to be out of the house when Haskett came to see the child. <break time="0.8s" /> Crowded into the elevated train, he found himself pressed against a tall man, whom he recognized with a start as Gus Varick, his wifes second husband. <break time="0.8s" /> Varick politely mentioned that Sellers, Waythorns senior partner, was laid up with gout, and each man pretended that there was nothing awkward about their meeting. <break time="0.8s" /> At lunch in a crowded restaurant, Waythorn noticed Varick at a table nearby, sipping a glass of brandy and then pouring the rest into his coffee. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a small habit, hardly worth noticing, yet Waythorn could not help watching him, as if the man knew things about Alice that he himself did not know. <break time="0.8s" /> That evening, as Alice poured the after dinner coffee, she added a little cognac to his cup without thinking, and handed it to him with a smile. <break time="0.8s" /> I do not take cognac in my coffee, Waythorn said lightly, and Alice, suddenly realizing her mistake, exclaimed, Oh, how stupid of me, and blushed a deep red. <break time="0.8s" /> The meaning of her blush was painfully clear to Waythorn, for the habit that she had remembered so naturally belonged to her second husband.
